state.task: Review how destructive schema transitions should be declared in canlang. AI agents generate this SaaS CRUD/workflow language targeting workerd and Cloudflare. Priorities are adoption, sparse repetition and a sole canonical primitive. Destructive migrations must be explicit, while source wrappers/manifests, schema duplication, arbitrary SQL/JS and validation frameworks are disallowed. Investigation plus specification adoption is authorized, provided demonstrated invalidity stops the proposal. There are no parsing/compilation/runtime implementations, installed predecessor facts, Git history or executed behavior checks here. Illustrative TeamTasks identifiers below are not historical deployment evidence. Classifier agreement cannot prove correctness or authorize an action.
state.existing: Ownership is by named package or the small app's implicit package name. File location contributes no identity/order; local selections deduplicate, and remote-bound imports expose only schemas. Every owner has ordered Given/When/Then sections. Records keep protected identifiers/team/parent and version/history attribution/archive metadata. by denotes callable operations, on trusted sources. Typed pure expressions and require/do/let/if/set are available. The for work limit is a rejection bound, not pagination. Fenced D1 and separate DO transactions explicitly exclude atomic authority transfers. Existing pre-state locks deny protected modification and removal, apart from declared expired disposal. Archived and physically retained expired records still participate in referential/unique constraints. The change-ownership section lists explicit destructive and meaning/backfill migration obligations but omits syntax; optional/default additions and indexes are currently called automatic too broadly.
state.boundary: A top-level migration Owner from="<installed-owner-snapshot-id>" would identify a logical declaration owner, leaving physical authority separate and creating no duplicate package name. Place it alongside real business source; after a complete implicit body it forms another top-level boundary. Partial Given/When/Then bodies remain errors. Derive relevance from desired local inclusion and actual old local removals; ignore other discovered transitions and bound-service providers. A When-local named migration keeps existing section/import locality, but whole-owner deletion calls for an additional declaration boundary or needless empty shell. A generated deployment plan offers smaller DSL files and familiar provider output; reviewed intent/transformation authoring moves to another channel. Merely inspecting compiler output requires neither a manifest nor repeated schema definitions. Keeping this issue open is another option.
state.versions: Use a compiler-created immutable content-addressed owner snapshot for from, including the prior canonical schema/rules, language version, resolved binding/routing and stored declaration contracts. Retain release/queued-contract metadata independently because unchanged tables can host changed handlers. Derive the target from present declarations; omit migration content from that fingerprint and separately identify transformation content and generated progress/apply records. Consume each installed logical owner once through retention, explicit one-to-one prefix rename or drop; give a target no more than one old source. Combine all applicable owner transitions into the derived deployment plan, with shared baselines not treated as conflicts by themselves. Permit only one exact selected edge for a given owner and from state. Missing historical snapshot, divergent baseline, collisions, overlapping consumption or ambiguity prevents upgrade. Keep applied transition bodies and target identities immutable. Authored source may hold current source alternatives; generated history carries completed transitions, without per-app counters or timestamp naming conventions. Initial install needs only current empty schema, parses present syntax/targets and cannot certify the inactive old-state bodies it did not typecheck.
state.mapping: An explicit rename associates old before.Model[.field] with a target model/field, and drop names removal. Preserve unchanged fields verbatim and initialize only compatible absent-null or independent constant defaults. backfill TargetModel supplies immutable per-row before and a partially initialized row of the desired type. Leading require plus do retains the ordered pure let/check/if/else/set-row grammar. Definitely assign missing required fields before any read and on every completing branch; derives remain unassignable. Exclude ambient actor/clock/random, provider work, hooks/operation calls, global collections and other-record reads. Allow old stored value components/opaque record identities; a reference reaches a target only through known retained/renamed identity and unchanged authority scope. Generated resumable staging must exhaust the frozen old dataset rather than reuse a bounded for loop as if it continued. Outputs never feed another input row. This intentionally does not cover record splitting, merging, old-data population of new models, parent/team/physical namespace moves or unconstrained job payload transformations. New models start with no records. Expression recipes remove body verbosity but need a new conditional expression for enum branching; migration scenarios reuse familiar effects at the cost of defining old/desired typing and exhaustive bounded execution.
state.safety: The rename owner directive associates exact old logical prefix with the header target, keeping physical routing/authority, teams/parents, record/file identities and role assignment. The drop owner case is legal only with target absent. They provide neither public compatibility aliases nor cross-deployment/class transfers; remote interface installation remains coordinated separately. Original locks still protect original pre-state values: name mappings keep them, but editing/deleting protected evidence fails. New protected fields get initialized before new locks begin. Include archives without unarchiving and never read/reconstruct expired content; affected incompatible disposal backlog must finish under its existing lifecycle. Target-wide invariants/lifetime and all retained reference/unique constraints remain requirements. A rename without value changes leaves content versions intact. Initialization/conversion of stored data, even automatic constant/null filling, advances each affected row once and records trusted maintenance attribution; queued version bindings may then be incompatible. Carry grants only into valid retained role mappings, blocking or explicitly reconciling deleted/changed-role assignments. Dropping schema is not complete audit/receipt/external erasure; retention and replay metadata still govern. Preserve R2 file identities/bytes, committing relationship release before retryable collection.
state.execution: These transitions are maintenance declarations outside by/on/export/UI/MCP and never run merely because compilation/discovery succeeds. Stop affected admissions, runtime writes, cleanup and dispatch; freeze source data, prepare the complete desired stage in bounded resumable work, check it, then activate. Preparation failure keeps the old selected release/data intact. Cross-authority activation may be partial, so keep affected access closed and resume safely rather than reopening against mixed versions; it is not atomic global rollback. DO coverage must come from authoritative inventory, not the eventual directory, with unavailable guarantees blocking rollout. Old runtimes cannot write the replaced layout. Incompatible queued contracts need drain/reconciliation or explicit invalidate before.handler of an inventoried asynchronous old handler. Only undispatched occurrences/intents receive recorded skipped migration outcomes, and their replay identities persist. External in-flight/accepted/uncertain work requires compatible reconciliation instead of false cancellation. Resolve every actual historical release/occurrence contract, including ones preceding the immediate baseline; lack of metadata blocks. Preserve completed receipt identities/schema/safe outcomes without replayed execution. Interface revision makes earlier sealed actions unusable. No zero-downtime or multi-owner transaction guarantee is supplied.
state.classification: Empty model creation, independent nullable/constant field additions and nonunique query indexes can be automatic only after full stored-state validity and ownership/reference/history/lock preservation. A server actor, random/current-time or historical-business default is not a historical backfill source. New uniqueness, stricter rules/types/enum sets, stored-to-derived change, data-meaning transformations and ownership changes need authored transitions. Changed creation defaults do not retroactively rewrite data. Storage compatibility is independent of tool/browser, bound service and queued-contract compatibility. Calendar snapshots in Member, the year field in Leave and raw files in Catch have unknown installed shapes/business history; this task must not invent old versions or their missing input data. A document can show a hypothetical predecessor/target and placeholder artifact, while real .can app transitions wait for actual predecessor evidence.
state.research: D1's primary migration documentation describes ordered SQL artifacts and applied history, which a compiler may generate. Its batch documentation promises sequence rollback, not rollout-wide atomicity. SQLite ALTER restrictions and table rebuilding show why target checks are needed; latest engine capabilities cannot be assumed for Cloudflare. Current Durable Object exports control class lifecycle namespaces, not row conversion or atomic arbitrary ownership movement. Consulted sources: https://developers.cloudflare.com/d1/reference/migrations/ ; https://developers.cloudflare.com/d1/worker-api/d1-database/ ; https://www.sqlite.org/lang_altertable.html ; https://developers.cloudflare.com/durable-objects/reference/durable-objects-migrations/ . This evidence does not establish implementation correctness.

boundary.instructions: What placement best expresses these maintenance changes through one route, including disappearance of a logical owner?

criteria.top_level_owner: Reference the owner in a top-level exact-baseline transition, paying for new discovery boundaries while supporting owner removal.
criteria.package_when: Keep named transitions within the owner's When block, retaining local scope but extending removal placement or maintaining a shell.
criteria.deployment_plan: Author no migration declarations in the DSL and use generated reviewed plans with a distinct explicit mapping channel.
criteria.unresolved: Do not settle placement if all presented mechanisms remain insufficient.

mapping.instructions: Which bounded typed mapping representation provides the best tradeoff of branching, compactness and existing syntax?

criteria.row_mapper: Use backfill with prior/desired row views and ordered pure checks, branches and assignments under require/do.
criteria.field_expression: Express field recipes directly, supplementing the language with conditional expressions.
criteria.maintenance_scenario: Extend maintenance scenarios with old/desired typing and exhaustive budgeted execution semantics.
criteria.unresolved: Leave value transformation open when the candidate forms cannot satisfy the constraints.

coherence.instructions: Are exact predecessor binding, one-to-one identity, preserved locks/files/expiry, complete-stage activation and historical-work dispositions consistent in this top-level row subset with unsupported transfers excluded?
